assumptions: a and b are strictly positive real constants in this finite analytic toy
Gamma_plus is a declared open rapid-decay toy ray, not an element of a specified relative-homology group and not a derived physical initial lapse cycle
the principal branch cut is excluded by the positive two-slab domain
the coordinate map (r_1,r_2) to (T,s) is used only for positive-domain bookkeeping and has no claim of a BV-BFV quantum pushforward
no gravitational field, ghost continuum, conformal factor, endpoint polarization, or absolute measure is supplied

declared_scope_guards.statement: Gamma_plus orientation is an input convention for this toy open ray.
The inequalities r_1,r_2,T>0 and 0<s<1 are declared hypotheses; the executable check verifies the inverse formulas and Jacobian, not the inequalities themselves.
No relative-homology group/class, physical lapse cycle, or gravity cycle is selected.
The cited BV-BFV sources frame classical boundary compatibility only and do not supply this toy ray, a quantum pushforward, or an absolute measure.

declared_toy.branch: principal Log on C minus (-infinity,0]; principal sqrt(N)=exp(Log(N)/2)
declared_toy.declared_open_rapid_decay_ray: Gamma_plus: N=r for r in (0,infinity), oriented from 0_plus to +infinity; no relative-homology group or class is asserted
declared_toy.endpoint_data: only the two decay ends 0_plus and +infinity of the declared ray; no Stokes coefficients or global relative-homology basis

exact_checks.statement: on the declared ray, exp(-(a/r+b*r)) decays at both stated ends for a,b>0
the forward and inverse coordinate formulas compose algebraically and det(partial(r_1,r_2)/partial(T,s))=-T; positivity is a separate declared-domain guard
the principal square-root product and its (T,s) coordinate form agree on the positive domain without crossing the cut

primary_sources.not_used_for: a selected lapse relative cycle, a quantum measure, or a continuum determinant line
primary_sources.source: Cattaneo and Schiavina, BV-BFV approach to General Relativity, Einstein-Hilbert action (2016)

primary_sources.not_used_for: a quantum contour theorem or a gravity absolute measure
primary_sources.source: Cattaneo and Mnev, A note on gluing via fiber products in the (classical) BV-BFV formalism (2023)
primary_sources.used_for: the requirement to keep compatible boundary data under a classical gluing model
